extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners learning historical arithmetic algorithms (medieval/early-modern arithmetic)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted procedural rules and heuristics for performing multiplication and division as described in a historical Italian arithmetic treatise (many 'modi' — first, second, etc.). Focuses on repeated replication, partitioning, alignment, carrying, tables of multiples, and several division approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat-the-figure multiplication (replication)
rubrics_metrics.description: «tante volte $te repfèta la figura» — multiply by repeating the figure as many times as the multiplier indicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the figure and repeat it the specified number of times; use repeated copies to form the product. Surrounding text advises careful placement in the margin and attention to lines to avoid mistakes (e.g., 'vedi i margine: poni d numero ve le iiolte... tira le righe ... nò abaglialTe'). Example/anti-pattern: failing to align repeated copies leads to wrong aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication by parts (decompose and recombine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decompose numbers into parts (partiti / partito) and multiply each part separately, then recombine the partial products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly recommends partitioning a number into convenient parts and multiplying each (e.g., 'partito... la parte... fa... contiene'), then summing the results. It explains grouping units and tens (and higher place-values) and treating each part according to its weight. Use this when direct replication is unwieldy; choose partitions that simplify multiplication (e.g., factors like 2,5,10, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tables of multiples and shift by place value (via powers of ten)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use precomputed multiples and shift according to the number of places (powers of ten) — many tabular examples like '9876 via 7 ... 52 ... 69i ...' illustrate using multiples and shifting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise shows making and consulting multiples (tables) and then placing/ shifting them by place (e.g., 'multiplica ... via ...'), effectively using multiplication by 10^k to align partial products. Advice: build tables for frequent multipliers and move the table result left/right according to place value rather than recomputing each time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and columnar placement (margine, righe)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place numbers in the margin and draw lines/rows to align digits and repeated figures (e.g., 'vedi i margine: poni d numero ... tira le righe').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful column alignment prevents errors in adding partial products and carrying. The text repeatedly instructs how to arrange rows of repeated figures, to 'poni' numbers and lines so the positions correspond to place values. Anti-pattern: misaligned rows leading to incorrect summation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry/aggregate by taking penultimate and earlier digits
rubrics_metrics.description: When combining partial results, take the penultimate (ferrare la penultima) and then proceed to earlier digits to carry and adjust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example instruction: 'ferrare la penultima del ... poi piglia la requète dopo' — i.e., secure the penultimate digit and then take the next for carrying. Use systematic carrying from right to left; when sums exceed a place, move the excess to the next column as described. The treatise gives multi-step examples of taking penultimate, then preceding figures to form correct final digits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross/lattice-like arrangement (use of 'croci' / 'croce')
rubrics_metrics.description: Form crosses or 'croci' and perform multiplicative intersections to obtain partial products (references to making 'croci' and 'croci còrno').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author advises making crosses and arranging multiplicative intersections similar to a lattice or cross method: 'farai vna croci ... poi cometa ... de la croce' to distribute and combine partial products. Guidance: form the cross patterns for regular distribution of partial products and then sum along diagonals/appropriate aggregates as illustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplying by repeated doubling/halving and known multipliers (use of factors like 2,3,5 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiply by iteratively using easier multipliers (doubling, tripling, etc.) and combining results — e.g., repeatedly doubling or applying sequences 'via 2, via 3, via 5 ...' to build the desired multiple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise shows obtaining complex multiples by composing simpler ones (e.g., get ×23 by combining ×20 and ×3). Guidance: choose decompositions into small multipliers that have easy tables (2,3,5,10) and assemble final product from those partial multiples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division by repeated subtraction/partitioning (multiple division methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple division modes are given: partition the dividend into parts corresponding to the divisor, subtract repeatedly, or use partitioning into units/grades — 'tutti li modi ... divisione' and many 'modi' enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author presents several division techniques (repeated subtraction, partition into units, hierarchical partitioning by place-value, using multiples and tables). Choose the method by convenience and size of numbers; the text emphasizes methods that avoid backtracking and that are 'piu sicuro'. Examples include dividing by assembling groups (1,2,5,10 patterns) and using previously computed multiples to subtract large chunks at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer reliable, less error-prone methods (avoid backtracking)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text repeatedly recommends selecting methods that are secure and less fallacious — choose the way that avoids returning backwards and reduces error (e.g., 'quella còrno ... è piu falda c fecura ... in ogni parte ... mai falla').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple valid methods exist, prefer the one described as more 'sicuro' (safe) and that minimizes corrections. The treatise notes some methods 'non falla' (do not fail) and suggests adopting them especially when numbers are large or when aggregation is complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mnemonic/ordered arrangements of digits (groupings like 1,2,5, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange digits into convenient ordered families or groups (series of units like 1,2,5,10 and sequences 1,2,3,4,5...) to facilitate multiplication/division rules and patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author shows arranging units in repeated structured orders to ease repeated operations and to recognize patterns (e.g., sequences and tables listed). Use these groupings to reduce cognitive load and speed repetitive computations; the text lists many numeric sequences as exemplars and prescribes applying the same operations to each grouped unit.
